Runner's Nutrition

Evidence-based nutrition strategies for training, racing and recovery. Use the calculator to build your personalized fueling plan.

Fueling Calculator
Get a personalized fueling plan based on Jeukendrup 2014 and ACSM guidelines.
Daily Training Nutrition

A runner's daily nutrition should be tailored to training volume and intensity. The following recommendations are based on the IOC consensus, Burke et al. (2011) and the 2025 update by Witard et al. (Sports Medicine), which revises runner protein needs upward.

Light training (30-60 min/day)3-5 g carbs/kg, 1.4-1.6 g protein/kg, 1 g fat/kg
Moderate training (60-90 min/day)5-7 g carbs/kg, 1.6-1.8 g protein/kg, 1-1.2 g fat/kg
Heavy training (90-120+ min/day)7-10 g carbs/kg, 1.8-2.0 g protein/kg, 1-1.5 g fat/kg
Double session or ultra10-12 g carbs/kg, 2.0-2.2 g protein/kg, 1.5 g fat/kg
Rest daysKeep protein at 2.0+ g/kg (repair continues)

Fat should not drop below 20% of total caloric intake to maintain hormone production and absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

  • •Spread protein across 4 servings of 0.3-0.4 g/kg every 3-4 h (Areta 2013): muscle protein synthesis increases by 31 to 48% vs 1-2 large meals. 25-30 g per meal hits the leucine threshold.
  • •Casein before bed (40 g cottage cheese or Greek yogurt): feeds muscles all night (Trommelen 2023).
  • •Favor complex carbs (rice, pasta, sweet potatoes, oats) outside the peri-exercise window.
  • •Include heme iron sources (red meat, organ meats) 2-3 times per week, especially for female runners.
  • •Ensure omega-3 intake through fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) 2-3 times per week.

Baseline hydration: aim for 30-35ml/kg/day outside training. Check urine color: pale yellow = well hydrated.

Key micronutrients for runners: vitamin D (especially in winter, aim for 1000-2000 IU/day if deficient), calcium (1000-1300mg/day for bone health), iron (monitor ferritin, optimal threshold > 30-50 ng/ml), magnesium (300-400mg/day).

Avoid Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S). Insufficient caloric intake impairs performance, bone health, immunity, and hormones. If you are losing weight unintentionally, consult a sports dietitian.
